items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Well Dave liked that particularly, the wonderful players like Eddie Lang and Bix Beiderbecke, the Dorseys, and Miff Mole.

ctx.x: It was almost just like rock & roll.

Exactly. That’s what I’m saying. It was the young people’s thing. And I think the same thing was in America too, you know, kids jiving and stuff like that in 1938, except it was, you had the thing here at source. We had to make to do with records, and make do with that. But that was wonderful. And 78s, luckily I lived at the time in a little part of London, south, in Streatham, we had a wonderful jazz record store there. They called it the Swing Shop. And the guy that ran it, Dave Carey, was a discographer, he…

they’re fabulous too. These guys were wonderful instrumentalists, but they were also, in the 20s, they were working like crazy. They were running from one recording date to another, running from one radio show to another, because radio was so big then in the 1920s. And that’s where I got to hear that kind of side to it too. And I loved that as well. But I remember when the LP came in, that was marvelous, because you had to really save your pennies to buy an LP, and then do you remember the little EPs that came…
